## Report: same pattern elsewhere

The inline-`composeRefs` pattern (calling `composeRefs(...)` during render, producing a new function identity every render) appears at **3 additional sites**:

- `dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.tsx:116` — `ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)}`
- `menu/src/menu.tsx:1056` — `ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)}`
- `navigation-menu/src/navigation-menu.tsx:1081` — `ref={composeRefs(ref, (node) => … setContent(node))}`

**But none of them are the same bug.** Why:

- **dropdown-menu & menu**: the unstable `composeRefs` value is passed as a `ref` into a downstream component (`Slot`, `MenuItemImpl`, `NavigationMenuContentImpl`) that internally composes via `useComposedRefs`. The function that actually lands on the DOM as a ref is that downstream **stable** composed ref; the upstream unstable function is just a value it reads once. I verified empirically: a state-setting ref through `DropdownMenu.Trigger` and `Menu.SubTrigger` does **not** loop (bounded render count).
- **navigation-menu**: same downstream absorption, but it's the one case that actually *relies* on the re-invocation-on-identity-change to re-call `setContent(node)` when the active content changes, so the viewport re-sizes to the active content. That re-invocation only works because the setter is idempotent (same node → React bails, no loop).

## What I did

I first changed `useComposedRefs` to a globally-stable callback — that fixed slot but **regressed navigation-menu**: its viewport would no longer update the observed `content` node on content switch (stable ref ⇒ no re-invocation ⇒ wrong resize target). I confirmed upstream `main` deliberately keeps `useComposedRefs` **unstable** and only fixes **slot** to use it (`useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`, with stable `forwardedRef` in the reported scenario ⇒ stable composed ref).

So I **reverted** the compose-refs change and kept only the slot fix — matching upstream, with zero side effects on the other packages.

## Files changed (final)

- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` — switched from `composeRefs` to `useComposedRefs`; moved the call **above** the摸底 the empty-children early return so hook order is stable when a Slot toggles empty↔populated.
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — added the React-19 loop regression test + the no-forwardedRef pass-through test.
- `.changeset/loud-cups-repeat.md` — slot-only patch changeset.

- Slot typecheck passes.
- navigation-menu/dropdown/menu are **not** the same bug, so left unchanged (per "fix only if same bug").

Wall time: 1.78 seconds

Done. Findings and resolution below.

## Report: same pattern elsewhere

The inline-`composeRefs` pattern (calling `composeRefs(...)` during render, producing a new function identity every render) appears at **3 additional sites**:

- `dropdown-menu/src/dropdown-menu.tsx:116` — `ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, context.triggerRef)}`
- `menu/src/menu.tsx:1056` — `ref={composeRefs(forwardedRef, subContext.onTriggerChange)}`
- `navigation-menu/src/navigation-menu.tsx:1081` — `ref={composeRefs(ref, (node) => … setContent(node))}`

**But none of them are the same bug.** Why:

- **dropdown-menu & menu**: the unstable `composeRefs` value is passed as a `ref` into a downstream component (`Slot`, `MenuItemImpl`, `NavigationMenuContentImpl`) that internally composes via `useComposedRefs`. The function that actually lands on the DOM as a ref is that downstream **stable** composed ref; the upstream unstable function is just a value it reads once. I verified empirically: a state-setting ref through `DropdownMenu.Trigger` and `Menu.SubTrigger` does **not** loop (bounded render count).
- **navigation-menu**: same downstream absorption, but it's the one case that actually *relies* on the re-invocation-on-identity-change to re-call `setContent(node)` when the active content changes, so the viewport re-sizes to the active content. That re-invocation only works because the setter is idempotent (same node → React bails, no loop).

## What I did

I first changed `useComposedRefs` to a globally-stable callback — that fixed slot but **regressed navigation-menu**: its viewport would no longer update the observed `content` node on content switch (stable ref ⇒ no re-invocation ⇒ wrong resize target). I confirmed upstream `main` deliberately keeps `useComposedRefs` **unstable** and only fixes **slot** to use it (`useComposedRefs(forwardedRef, slottableElementRef)`, with stable `forwardedRef` in the reported scenario ⇒ stable composed ref).

So I **reverted** the compose-refs change and kept only the slot fix — matching upstream, with zero side effects on the other packages.

## Files changed (final)

- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.tsx` — switched from `composeRefs` to `useComposedRefs`; moved the call **above** the摸底 the empty-children early return so hook order is stable when a Slot toggles empty↔populated.
- `packages/react/slot/src/slot.test.tsx` — added the React-19 loop regression test + the no-forwardedRef pass-through test.
- `.changeset/loud-cups-repeat.md` — slot-only patch changeset.

## Verification
- `pnpm vitest run packages/react/slot` → 31 passed, 2 skipped (pre-existing skips).
- `pnpm vitest run packages/react` → 257 passed, 2 skipped, 1 todo — no regressions.
- Slot typecheck passes.
- navigation-menu/dropdown/menu are **not** the same bug, so left unchanged (per "fix only if same bug").
